dedupe_keys.name: automated vehicles and parking in the san francisco central business district sumo scenarios of drop off travel

description: This study simulated how automated vehicles that drop off and pick up passengers instead of parking would change traffic flow, vehicle miles travelled and greenhouse gas emissions in the central business district of San Francisco. Scenarios varied the share of drop-off and pick-up travel against parking, the supply of on-street and off-street parking, and demand responses to a large change in the price of curbside space. The team ran the SUMO microscopic traffic simulator on an OpenStreetMap network of the district's major roads and 45 traffic analysis zones, with an average weekday of travel from the San Francisco Bay Area MATSim model (about 900,000 travellers and 1.8 million trips touching the area), calibrated with the regional activity-based model of the Metropolitan Transportation Commission, and parking supply from the San Francisco parking census of the SFMTA. It was carried out at the University of California, Davis, with funding from the California Department of Transportation, and the full model inputs, scenario sets, outputs and plots are free to download from Dryad (25 March 2020, 3.5 GB, CC0). Coverage is city scale for one district and one weekday. Outcome: the release provides traffic, queue and emission outputs for every scenario; the findings are in the project report, which was not read. Limitations: minor roads are left out, and trips were adjusted to network supply. The case shows policy evaluation of curb and parking management with SUMO and MATSim, both catalogued here.
